title: Command Injection in Kubelet /logs API via Pattern Parameter on Windows
analysis:
The Kubelet `/logs` endpoint on Windows nodes contains a command injection vulnerability due to insufficient sanitization/validation of the user-provided `pattern` query parameter. 

When a log query is made with a pattern, `newNodeLogQuery` in `pkg/kubelet/kubelet_server_journal.go` stores this query parameter in `nlq.Pattern`. The only validation performed on this string is a syntax check to ensure it is a valid regular expression:
```go
if _, err := syntax.Parse(n.Pattern, syntax.Perl); err != nil { ... }
```
This check is insufficient as patterns containing single quotes, semicolons, and other script separators (e.g., `foo'; calc.exe; #`) are valid regular expressions.

On Windows, the `getLoggingCmd` function in `pkg/kubelet/kubelet_server_journal_windows.go` constructs a PowerShell command using string formatting:
```go
psCmd += fmt.Sprintf(" | Where-Object -Property Message -Match '%s'", n.Pattern)
```
This string is then executed using `PowerShell.exe` with the `-Command` flag, which parses the string and executes it as code. Because the input single quotes are not escaped or removed, an attacker can break out of the single-quoted string context and inject arbitrary PowerShell command blocks.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
To execute a command on the target Windows node, a user authorized to query the Kubelet `/logs` API can send a request to:
`/logs?query=kubelet&pattern=test%27%3b+Start-Process+calc.exe%3b+%23`

The generated PowerShell command will be parsed and executed as:
`Get-WinEvent ... | Where-Object -Property Message -Match 'test'; Start-Process calc.exe; #' | ...`
This causes PowerShell to execute the `Start-Process calc.exe` command with system/kubelet privilege on the Windows host.
